data.finding: On this attempt the left stick return changed from 136/126 before the single circular movement to 127/126 before cardinal movements, then 128/126 after them. The right stick had 135/121 after one cardinal sequence and 134/120 after the repeat, without a circular movement in the observed capture.
limits: Capture starts at adapter report sequence 69, not at power-on; previous input before this point is not observed.
Single-circle angle estimate calculated from protocol coordinates about 128/128, not a physical rotation sensor.
First circle return window is shorter than later three-second windows because next movement followed quickly.
No independent physical neutral-position witness.
Treatment is confounded with stick identity: left received circle plus directions, right directions alone. This does not establish circles are universally better than directions.

movementSummary.right: One approximately 1.074-turn clockwise circular movement, then up/right/down/left; circle and four-direction returns both 133/122.
movementSummary.left: First sequence up/down/right/left, then additional up/right/left/down/right movements; no circular movement detected. First four-direction return 127/128; final return after additional right movement 122/127.

data.finding: This reversed attempt does not reproduce a rule that circle gives a better center than cardinal directions. Left reached 127/128 with directions alone; right reached 133/122 after the circle, not closer to 128/128 than its pre-circle 130/134. Later left return changes show movement-history dependence.
limits: One segment only. USB reset was requested, but its physical disconnect/reconnect was outside the recorded stream or not observed.
Initial report sequence 1520 is lower than prior attempt final 15842, compatible with counter reset between recordings, not direct evidence of its cause.
First left direction order differs from requested up/right/down/left; there were five extra directional bouts. Do not compare only final values as a matched four-direction treatment.
Physical neutral is not independently measured; short return windows follow detected movements.
Rotation is an estimate from 8-bit protocol coordinates about 128/128.
Physical release is inferred from movement followed by stable coordinates, with operator-confirmed completion, not an independent mechanical witness.
One circle is operator reported. Native trajectory spans both axes from 0 to 255; signed arc estimate is sensitive to release path and not an independent physical turn count.
First right-direction sequence was right/up/down/left; second up/right/down/left. Compare matching directions, preserving sequence history.
First recorded report sequence 81; startup polls before enumeration are not captured.
Returned coordinates are protocol outputs, not unprocessed ADC voltages.
data.interpretation: Right first-series direction-dependent return spread shrinks substantially in its second series. Left returns after the reported circle remain tightly grouped in its first cardinal series. This supports movement-history-dependent adaptation and is the appropriate per-return comparison; terminal centers alone obscure it. Exact internal calibration formula and whether the circle itself caused the left stability are not directly resolved.

findings: Left movements precede right movements. Protocol values do not reach 0 or 255 on any axis.
Stable pauses between movements have different coordinates; final coordinates also differ from initial recorded values.
All four axes remain exactly unchanged for the final 28.3 seconds. No continuing convergence toward 128/128 is observed during this final stationary interval.
limits: Stable protocol plateaus may be released positions or held small deflections. Individual releases were not separately marked or mechanically witnessed.
Micro is an operator description; movement amplitude here is measured only in protocol units, not physical angle.
Prior capture ended at sequence 26410, current capture starts at 67855. Movement during this recording gap is not known; do not assign gap changes to this trial.
Center variation following micro movements alone does not distinguish mechanical return hysteresis from internal correction.
